about: Native rewrites for poteto-mode playbooks, references, and scripts. See docs/claude-code-mapping.md.

edits.find:
# Bugbot triage

Use this reference when the Babysit playbook (`../playbooks/babysit.md`) handles Bugbot or review-automation comments. The goal is not to ignore Bugbot by default.
edits.replace:
# Review-bot triage

Use this reference when the Babysit playbook (`../playbooks/babysit.md`) handles review-bot comments. On GitHub they are ordinary review threads from accounts such as `cursor[bot]` (Bugbot), `claude[bot]`, CodeRabbit, or Copilot. The goal is not to ignore a bot by default.
edits.why: A Claude Code user gets review comments from several bots, not only Cursor's Bugbot. The skeptical triage applies to every one of them.

edits.replace: Classify each review-bot thread before acting:
edits.why: The rubric covers every review bot.

edits.why: The pattern holds for any review bot.

edits.replace: Each owner is a subagent with `isolation: "worktree"` and a brief that names its branch off current trunk. The owner builds,

edits.find: Assume the VM dies. Soon after starting, push and start a decision trail in the root agent's store (path in the system prompt) per the **show-me-your-work** skill, then push each finished unit before you start the next.
edits.replace: Assume the owner dies, because a subagent ends with the session that runs it. Soon after starting, push and start a decision trail in the root's store per the **show-me-your-work** skill, then push each finished unit before you start the next. The root's store is `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/omc-pstack-fy/`, where `<slug>` is the root's workspace path with every character that is not a letter or digit changed to `-`. Every brief names that absolute path.
edits.why: Claude Code names no agent store in the system prompt, and an owner in a worktree has a different workspace path from the root.

edits.find: (such as `control-ui` or `control-cli` from `cursor-team-kit`)
edits.replace: (such as `control-ui` or `control-cli`)

edits.find: One verifier per PR, each a Cursor cloud agent, runs the change the way a user would with the matching control skill (such as `control-ui` or `control-cli` from `cursor-team-kit`), parent against head,
edits.replace: One verifier per PR, each a subagent with `isolation: "worktree"` at that PR's head, runs the change the way a user would with the matching control skill (such as `control-ui` or `control-cli`), parent against head,
edits.why: Claude Code has no cloud agents. A worktree subagent keeps each verifier on its own checkout. omc-pstack-fy bundles control-ui and control-cli.

edits.find: 5. **Spawn one blinded judge** on a different model family per the **arena** skill's Phase C.
edits.replace: 5. **Spawn one blinded judge** as the **arena** skill's Phase C does, but take its model from the `second opinion` line. Prefer an entry on a different vendor from yours, else a different model, such as opus against sonnet. When every entry shares your model, use the no-line rule below. An external judge runs read-only through the **pstack-ask** skill. Its throwaway copy of the repository does not reach the candidates' dirs, so inline each output under its sanitized label. With no line, the judge runs on sonnet when you run on opus, and on opus otherwise. Name the panel in the reply. "Cross-vendor panel (claude, codex)" is stronger evidence than "same-vendor panel (opus, sonnet)".
edits.why: The second opinion line replaces a different model family, per the Phase 3 contract, and may name another vendor's model. With no line, a different Claude model is the closest match. Naming the panel keeps the reply from overstating the verdict.

edits.find: Read each candidate's local transcript under the active workspace's `agent-transcripts/` directory (the system prompt names this path). Do not glob across `~/.cursor/projects/*/`.
edits.replace: Find each candidate's transcript with `find ~/.claude/projects/<slug> -name 'agent-<id>.jsonl'`, where `<slug>` is this workspace's path with every character that is not a letter or digit changed to `-` and `<id>` is the agent id its spawn returned. Do not glob across `~/.claude/projects/*/`.
edits.why: Claude Code stores a subagent's transcript at ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<session>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl, and the system prompt does not name the folder.

edits.find: 1. Locate the prior trail. A local transcript under the active workspace's `agent-transcripts/` directory (the system prompt names the path. Do not glob across `~/.cursor/projects/*/`, that crosses workspace boundaries and reads private chats from unrelated projects), a cloud-agent URL, or a pushed branch. Read the metadata overview and last messages first, then scan back for the decision points.
edits.replace: 1. Locate the prior trail. It is a Claude Code transcript, a session id, or a pushed branch. Transcripts live in `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/`, where `<slug>` is this workspace's path with every character that is not a letter or digit changed to `-`. A session id names `<session-id>.jsonl` there, and its subagents' transcripts sit in `<session-id>/subagents/`. Without an id, the newest `.jsonl` other than this session's is the likely prior session, so confirm it against the user's description. Do not glob across `~/.claude/projects/*/`, because that crosses workspace boundaries and reads private chats from unrelated projects. Read the metadata lines, such as `ai-title`, and the last messages first, then scan back for the decision points. A human message is a `type: "user"` line with text content. A `tool_result` block is not one.
edits.why: Claude Code keeps transcripts in its own per-workspace folder, which the system prompt does not name, and a session id stands in for a cloud-agent URL.

edits.find: misses one that lives at `.cursor/worktrees/myrepo/x`
edits.replace: misses one that lives at `.claude/worktrees/x` inside the repo
edits.why: Claude Code puts the worktrees it creates under .claude/worktrees/ in the repository.

edits.find: The pinned and active chats are the real artifact (principle-prove-it-works). Get that set from the user or sidebar and cross-check every candidate. The lever has marked `safe` a worktree the user had pinned, so the pinned set wins.
edits.replace: The chats still in use are the real artifact (principle-prove-it-works). Get that set from the user and cross-check every candidate. The lever has marked `safe` a worktree a chat still needed, so the user's set wins.
edits.why: Claude Code has no sidebar of pinned chats, so the user names the chats still in use.

edits.find: report whether the chat is pinned or ongoing and which worktrees it touches (principle-guard-the-context-window, transcripts are bulk). A pinned chat spawns arena and repro trees into sibling worktrees via background subagents, and those are in use even when their names never hit the sidebar.
edits.replace: report whether the chat is still in use and which worktrees it touches (principle-guard-the-context-window, transcripts are bulk). A chat in use spawns arena and repro trees into sibling worktrees via background subagents, and those are in use even when only a subagent's transcript names them.
edits.why: Claude Code has no sidebar of pinned chats. A worktree subagent's path shows up in its own transcript under the parent session.

edits.find: 1. Use the **create-skill** skill (Cursor's built-in for authoring SKILL.md files).
edits.replace: 1. Use the `skill-creator` skill when the session lists it. Otherwise write `SKILL.md` with `name` and `description` frontmatter under `.claude/skills/<name>/`, or `~/.claude/skills/<name>/` for a personal skill.

edits.find:
# Transcripts dir: ~/.cursor/projects/<slugified-repo-path>/agent-transcripts.
slug=$(printf '%s' "$main_wt" | sed 's#^/##; s#/#-#g')
transcripts="$HOME/.cursor/projects/$slug/agent-transcripts"
edits.replace:
# Claude Code keeps transcripts in ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/, where the slug is
# the workspace path with every character that is not a letter or digit
# changed to -. The search is recursive, so it also reads
# <session>/subagents/, where worktree subagents log.
slug() { printf '%s' "$1" | sed 's/[^A-Za-z0-9]/-/g'; }
transcripts="$HOME/.claude/projects/$(slug "$main_wt")"
# Claude Code hands rg to its own shell as a function, which a script does not
# inherit, so fall back to grep.
if command -v rg >/dev/null 2>&1; then search="rg -l"; else search="grep -rl"; fi
edits.why: Claude Code stores transcripts under ~/.claude/projects/ with its own slug rule, and its bundled rg is not on a script's PATH.

edits.find: f=$(rg -l -e "${wt}/" -e "${wt}\"" "$transcripts" 2>/dev/null \
edits.replace: f=$($search -e "${wt}/" -e "${wt}\"" "$transcripts" "$HOME/.claude/projects/$(slug "$wt")" 2>/dev/null \
edits.why: A session started inside a worktree gets that worktree's own transcript folder, so a chat still in use there is not missed.

edits.find: Each tick re-reads this playbook from trunk and fixes drift,
edits.replace: Each tick re-reads poteto-mode's `SKILL.md` and this playbook from the newest installed omc-pstack-fy copy (the highest `version` under `~/.claude/plugins/cache/omc-pstack-fy/`), because a plugin user's repository has no pstack folder and a mid-run compaction keeps only part of them. It then fixes drift,
edits.why: A plugin user's repository has no pstack/ folder, so trunk holds no playbook. A long loop compacts, and compaction re-attaches only the first ~5,000 tokens of a skill.

edits.find: No event gets a fixed-interval heartbeat sized to when the result is worth re-checking.
edits.replace: No event gets a fixed-interval heartbeat sized to when the result is worth re-checking. Each wake first re-reads poteto-mode's `SKILL.md` and this playbook, because a mid-run compaction keeps only part of them.
edits.why: A long loop compacts, and compaction re-attaches only the first ~5,000 tokens of a skill, which cuts poteto-mode short and drops this playbook.

allow.why: Names Bugbot beside its GitHub account as one review bot among several, and keeps upstream's Bugbot track record in three evidence lines, because that history is one bot's, not every bot's.
